key_insight: Simulated quantum layers can improve vision-language accuracy or reduce trainable parameters, but benefits depend strongly on placement.
engineering_relevance: Selective quantum-layer integration offers a design path for hybrid VLMs, though parameter savings do not reliably reduce training time or computation.
method: Use LLaVA-OneVision with classically simulated 4- and 8-qubit circuits.
Test basic-ring and strongly entangling circuits at four insertion and four replacement locations.
Compare accuracy and computational cost, and evaluate robustness under six attack settings.
evidence_signal: On Visual Spatial Reasoning development data, post-projector insertion reaches 80.7% accuracy (+2.28 percentage points over classical full fine-tuning), while final decoder feed-forward replacement retains 79.22% with 13.07 million fewer trainable parameters.
watch_item: These simulation-based results do not establish quantum-hardware speedups, generalizable gains, or a security advantage.
paper_title: Can Quantum Layers offer Performance and Security Advantages in Vision-Language Models?
